newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mainly steady, gas oil gains.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mainly steady, gas oil gains.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly steady on Friday, but gas oil rose on futures strength, traders said.
Gasoline prices were steady in quiet trade with demand limited to small East Med requirements as European buyers stayed scarce, traders said.
Premium unleaded cargoes were assessed steady around $218 a tonne cif Med.
Naphtha prices were little changed and traders expected the market to track crude with little impetus to push the market either way next week.
"Effectively the market is balanced to long, but it's illiquid with few buyers and no aggressive sellers", one trader said.
Prompt cargoes were valued around $218 a tonne cif Med.
Physical fuel oil was quiet with most activity on swaps. January paper was done at $108, $108.25 and $108.50 fob Med.
"I think that's pretty close to the wet market, but there has been so little happening its hard to say," said one Med trader.
Low sulphur cracked fuel was also in the doldrums hovering broadly unchanged around $137 cif Med.
Gas prices rose $8.50 on futures strength.
That was triggered by European and U.S. cold weather forecasts and premiums continued to recover despite persistent length in Russians.
A cargo of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was done at high cif quotes -$0.10 cif Genoa, up from Thursday's traded level of cif high quotes -$0.25 cif Genoa.
Fob barrels for loading December 20-25 in west Med were around high cif -$8.75, equivalent to high cif quotes +$0.25 basis Genoa.
